name: Same-account SQS grant to an in-account role - a direct same-account grant, NOT cross-account or public
note: IAM-1207 (boundary of suite-2 test 32 semantics on SQS). An SQS queue in account 123456789012 grants sqs:SendMessage to a role in the SAME account. The account component of the queue ARN equals the principal's account, so this is a direct same-account resource grant (RESOURCE-SAME-ACCOUNT-GRANT, medium) with the resource-vs-identity caveat - it must NOT be flagged cross-account and must NOT be flagged public.
rationale: The SQS queue ARN carries an owning account (123456789012) and the named principal is a role in that SAME account, so the account comparison is decisive: this is a direct same-account resource-policy grant, not a cross-account one. Within a single account AWS evaluates the union of identity- and resource-based permissions, so a same-account resource-policy Allow can grant even when the principal's identity policy is silent - materially different from a cross-account grant where BOTH accounts must allow. That distinction is why RESOURCE-SAME-ACCOUNT-GRANT (medium) is correct here and RESOURCE-CROSS-ACCOUNT is wrong. A named IAM role is not '*', so PUBLIC-ACCESS must not fire; a role is not a service, so RESOURCE-CONFUSED-DEPUTY must not fire. An applicable explicit Deny in any layer still blocks. Ref: docs/resource-policy-semantics.md sec 1.1 / 7.2.
